hypotheses.name: QFaults-B transfer: the organisers' own second inventory as a new-fault prior
hypotheses.layers: USGS Quaternary Fault and Fold Database polylines (attributes SLIPRT2023, REC2023, SLIPSENSE, MAPSCALE, FTYPE) minus the pixels already covered by the training catalogue; features = distance to the nearest uncovered trace, recency-weighted and slip-rate-weighted
hypotheses.physical_signature: An independent, seismic-hazard-grade compilation of Quaternary surface rupture. Traces present in QFaults but absent from the training catalogue are, by definition, fault geometry the organiser's own label source contains and the training labels do not.
hypotheses.why_it_catches_a_missing_fault: The rules state the scored labels come from the USGS Quaternary Fault and Fold Database plus expert-identified new faults, while the training labels came from the INGENIOUS Great Basin compilation. Any QFault trace outside the training catalogue is therefore a direct member of the scored population rather than a proxy for it -- the strongest available prior on the final-round reward.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Sibling lanes rasterised the QFaults service only as a cross-catalogue transfer surrogate (fetch_qfaults.py) and used it to audit proxy-catalogue policy, not as a feature in a submission model. No lane restricted it to the complement of the training catalogue, and none weighted it by REC2023/SLIPRT2023.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: high (the only hypothesis that targets the scored inventory directly rather than a physical proxy for it)
hypotheses.implementation_cost: medium: one fetch from a documented public service, polyline rasterisation, complement mask, distance transform, then the same gated arm comparison used here

hypotheses.name: Thermal-fluid pathway layer (hot springs, well temperatures, geothermometry)
hypotheses.layers: GDR 'Well and Spring Temperature and Chemistry' table: measured temperature, quartz/chalcedony/cat geothermometer temperatures, thermal class, at 12,570 distinct grid cells; kernel density at a ~400 m scale
hypotheses.physical_signature: Fluid upflow and discharge. In the Basin and Range, hot springs sit on fault intersections and relay zones, so hot-site density is a map of permeable structure rather than of topography.
hypotheses.why_it_catches_a_missing_fault: Surface-rupture mapping requires a scarp; fluid pathways do not. Springs mark blind, buried and small-displacement structures that a surface-rupture catalogue under-maps, which is the same population the organisers' expert round adds.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: No lane in this family carries the spring/well temperature table as a model feature; it appears only as background knowledge in a research note.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: medium in principle, but measured NEGATIVE below
hypotheses.implementation_cost: low: local CSV, kernel density, one blended emission sweep

hypotheses.name: Drainage response: chi (chi) transformation and knickpoint density on the provided detrended-elevation band
hypotheses.layers: detrended elevation (official band 6) and its slope (band 7), plus the competition lidar scarps for valley identification; optional 3DEP 1/3 arc-second DEM as a coarse anchor
hypotheses.physical_signature: A channel crossing an active or recently active fault steps down; along-stream chi plots show a break, and knickpoint density anomalies trace the structure responsible even where no scarp was mapped.
hypotheses.why_it_catches_a_missing_fault: Fluvial networks integrate vertical motion over 10^4-10^5 yr, so they respond to structures that have insufficient surface expression to be mapped as a scarp but are nonetheless deforming the landscape.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Sibling lanes used elevation edges, curvature, Euler depth, tensor/strain and scarp morphology; none computed a stream network relative metric (chi, ksn, knickpoint density), which is a different observable from gradient products.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: high: flow routing over 12.3M cells plus network statistics; needs either pysheds/richdem from PyPI or a hand-rolled D8

hypotheses.name: Radiometric alteration ratios (K, eTh, eU) over the GeoDAWN survey
hypotheses.layers: GeoDAWN airborne radiometrics: potassium, equivalent thorium and uranium channels, as ratios (K/eTh, eU/eTh) and as a K-enrichment anomaly
hypotheses.physical_signature: Hydrothermal alteration: K metasomatism along fluid pathways, potassic clay alteration, and uranium enrichment in fracture damage zones produce a distinctive K-high / Th-low ratio.
hypotheses.why_it_catches_a_missing_fault: Alteration halos record where fluids moved in the past, which persists after the topographic scarp has been erased or buried -- so it can mark the location of a structure with no modern surface expression.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: One sibling lane used a radiometric edge-coherence diagnostic; no lane has used the K/Th/U ratio (alteration index) as a model feature.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: low-medium: the survey is already published as a GeoTIFF archive; the work is ratioing, resampling to 100 m and the standard gate

hypotheses.name: Seismicity geometry: depth-banded hypocentre density and focal-mechanism strike
hypotheses.layers: ANSS Comprehensive Catalog hypocentres (depth, magnitude) and focal mechanism solutions, projected to the grid; the official band 19 carries only 2-D earthquake density
hypotheses.physical_signature: Active structures concentrate seismicity on planes. A depth band (3-10 km) isolates crustal faults from quarry blasts and deep events, and mechanism nodal planes give the strike to correlate.
hypotheses.why_it_catches_a_missing_fault: Seismicity locates active structures regardless of surface expression, so a lineament defined by hypocentres is evidence of a fault the surface catalogue does not contain.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: The family used the provided 2-D density band; no lane has used depths, magnitudes or mechanisms to build a 3-D/structural feature.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: low-medium: the footprint's seismicity is sparse and clustered, so the field is noisy at 100 m
hypotheses.implementation_cost: medium: API paging with a footprint envelope query, declustering (Gardner-Knopoff or Reasenberg), then the standard gate
